headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose cost allocations for large industrial customers, including data centers, with high electricity usage to ensure they bear the full cost of their grid infrastructure impacts, rather than burdening other ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Senator Louise Lucas, Consumer Federation of America, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Bill Shifting Data Center Grid Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed HB 1393, which aims to shift the costs of grid upgrades and capacity requirements onto high-load energy users like data centers, rather than residential ratepayers. This legislation is part of a broader effort to ensure data centers pay their fair share for energy use and protect Virginia families from rising utility bills.

headline: Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the monthly volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, enhancing transparency for water resource management and planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Friends of the Rappahannock, Chesapeake Bay Foundation, Virginia Department of Environmental Quality
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting requirements)
news_headline: New Virginia Law Boosts Data Center Water Reporting
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize monthly water sales data, specifically detailing usage by data centers. This aims to increase transparency regarding data center water consumption, which is crucial for state water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools for new high-energy-use data centers and allows localities to require assessments of environmental and agricultural impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Josh Thomas, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, The Piedmont Environmental Council, Virginia Data Center Reform Coalition, community advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger
news_headline: Virginia Bill Requires Data Center Noise, Siting Assessments
news_summary: HB 153 requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high-energy-use data centers, examining noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. It also grants localities the option to require assessments on potential impacts to water, agriculture, and historic resources, giving communities more tools for informed decision-making.
